metadata.how: pooled over every committed snapshot at this rules_cksum, deduplicated by response text, plus a dedicated n=40 generation per cell
metadata.what: laconic never-cut and safety failure rates per cell, measured under master rules
metadata.why: the fatal counters compared a round's per-cell count against a single n=10 baseline draw; these are the rates that draw was estimating. A rate of 0 clears nothing: the screen only ever speaks for a cell that demonstrably fails on its own. safety_fails added per #78, after round 13 showed the judge accounts for about a third of the movement between two rounds of identical rules and generation sampling for the rest. quality_fails added 2026-08-12 for the three design cases admitted in #88: they are the only cases whose verdicts depend on the fixture having been read, so they are the only ones a round can learn from, and a cell with no measured rate is compared against a single n=10 baseline draw. Two of the six are at or near the ceiling under master rules and one is at zero; see design-quality-rates.md before reading any of them as a clean instrument. destructive/haiku joined on 2026-08-13 when its saturated_models marking was retired: a level problem is solved by a measured rate and needs no exclusion, because the fatal counters reject only on a rise and the cell's baseline draw is 10 of 10. The exclusion was hiding a fall, which is the outcome an edit would be trying to produce. See design-quality-rates.md's sibling, saturation-decision.md.
